q: 1. Stress is directly proportional to strain within elastic limit is given by
explain: This fundamental principle of elasticity was established by Robert Hooke.

q: 2. The stress necessary to initiate yielding, is considerably
options: more than that necessary to continue it
less than that necessary to continue it
more than that necessary to stop it
less than that necessary to stop it
explain: The upper yield point (stress to initiate yielding) is higher than the lower yield stress required to sustain/continue the yielding process.

q: 3. Stress in a member subjected to a force is
options: the ratio of modulus of elasticity to strain
the product of modulus of elasticity and strain
the resistance to the force acting
sum of strain and modulus of elasticity
explain: According to the constitutive relation σ = Eε, stress is the product of the modulus of elasticity and strain.

q: 4. The phenomenon of slow extension of materials having constant load, i.e. increasing with the time is called
explain: Creep is defined as the slow, time-dependent increase in strain of a material under a constant sustained load.

q: 5. Young's modulus is the ratio of the normal stress to the
options: reciprocal of normal strain within elastic limit
explain: Young's modulus is valid only within the proportional limit where the stress-strain curve is linear.

q: 6. Modulus of rigidity is the ratio of
explain: The modulus of rigidity (G) is the ratio of shear stress to the corresponding shear strain.

q: 7. Plasticity of a body is
options: the ratio of stress to strain
explain: While elasticity allows recovery of shape, plasticity is the property that allows permanent deformation.

q: 8. The ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain is called
explain: Poisson's ratio is a dimensionless constant representing the ratio of transverse contraction to longitudinal extension.

q: 9. The value of possion's ratio always remains
explain: For most engineering materials, Poisson's ratio typically ranges from 0 to 0.5, thus remaining less than one.

q: 10. If the stress in each cross-section of a pillar is equal to its working stress, it is called
explain: A 'body of equal strength' is one designed so that the stress is uniform (equal to the working/allowable stress) at every cross-section along its length.

q: 11. The property by which the metals deforms continuously at a slow rate without further increase in stress is called
explain: Creep is the time-dependent permanent deformation that occurs under constant stress, usually at high temperatures.

q: 12. The ratio of maximum instantaneous stress due to sudden loading to the maximum stress due to gradual loading will be
explain: Stress produced by a suddenly applied load is twice the stress produced by the same load applied gradually.

q: 13. The stress due to temperature change in a member depends on
explain: Thermal stress only develops if the expansion or contraction is restricted by the support conditions.

q: 14. The strain energy stored in a specimen when strained within the elastic limit is known as
explain: Resilience is the capacity of a material to absorb energy when it is deformed elastically.

q: 15. Find the modulus elasticity of bar material (E) if c/s area of bar is A, length L, applied load P and elongation is Δ
explain: Rearranging the elongation formula Δ = PL/AE to solve for E gives E = PL/AΔ.

q: 16. Elasticity of a body is
options: the property by which a body returns to its original shape after removal of the load
the ratio of stress to strain
the resistance to the force acting
large deformability as in case of rubber
explain: Elasticity is fundamentally defined as the ability of a material to return to its original shape/size once the deforming load is removed.

q: 17. As per elastic theory of design the factor of safety is the ratio of
options: unlimited load to load at yield.
explain: In elastic (working stress) design, factor of safety is defined as the ratio of the yield stress to the actual working (allowable) stress used in design.

q: 18. In a composite bar the load distribution among different materials of which it is made is based on the assumption that all the materials will have
explain: In a composite bar, since all constituent materials are rigidly connected and deform together, they undergo the same strain, and load distribution is derived from this compatibility condition.

q: 19. The elongation of conical bar under its own weight is equal to
options: that of prismatic bar of same length
one half that of a prismatic bar of same length
one third that of a prismatic bar of same length
one fourth that of a prismatic bar of same length
explain: Integrating the varying cross-section of a conical bar under self-weight gives an elongation equal to one-third of that of an equivalent prismatic bar of the same length.

q: 20. A strut is member which
options: is subjected to shear force predominantly
is subjected to axial compressive predominantly
is subjected to bending moment and shear force along with any axial force
explain: A strut is defined as a structural member primarily subjected to axial compressive force.

q: 21. Bulk Modulus, Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio are connected by the relation
explain: The standard elastic relation connecting Young's modulus E, bulk modulus K and Poisson's ratio (1/m) is E = 3K(1 − 2/m).

q: 22. The greatest eccentricity which a load W can have without producing tension on the cross-section of a short column of external diameter D and internal diameter d, is
explain: For a hollow circular column, the limiting eccentricity for no tension is derived from the section's core boundary, giving e = (D²+d²)/8D.

q: 23. The ratio of maximum and average shear stresses on a rectangular section is
explain: For a rectangular section, max shear stress = 1.5 × average shear stress (a standard parabolic distribution result), giving a ratio of 1.5.

q: 24. A bar of square section of area a² is held such that its one of its diameters is vertical; maximum shear stress will develop at a depth h where h is
explain: For a square section oriented with a diagonal vertical, the maximum shear stress occurs at a depth from the top vertex of 3√2·a/4 (with side a), matching option (b).

q: 25. The maximum stress produced in a bar of tapering section is at
explain: For a given axial load, stress = Force/Area, so the smaller cross-sectional area at the smaller end of a tapering bar experiences the maximum stress.

q: 26. Modular ratio of the two materials is the ratio of
explain: Modular ratio, used in composite section analysis, is defined as the ratio of the moduli of elasticity of the two materials involved.

q: 27. A rod is enclosed centrally in a tube and the assembly is tightened by rigid washers. If assembly is subjected to a compressive load, then
options: both rod and tube are under compression
tube is under tension and rod is under compression
explain: Since the rigid washers force the rod and tube to shorten together under the applied compressive load, both components share and resist the load in compression.

q: 28. When a bar of length l, width b and thickness t is subjected to a pull of P, its
options: length increases, width and thickness decreases
length decreases, width and thickness increases
explain: Under axial tension (a pull), the bar elongates (length increases) while due to Poisson's effect it contracts laterally (width and thickness decrease).

q: 29. What is tenacity?
explain: Tenacity is the technical term for the ultimate tensile strength of a material.

q: 30. A localized compressive stress at the area of contact between two members is known as
explain: A localized compressive stress at the contact area between two members (such as at a bearing or joint) is termed crushing (bearing) stress.

q: 31. Principle plane is a plane on which the shear stress is
explain: A principal plane is defined as a plane on which the shear stress is zero, and only normal (principal) stress acts.

q: 32. The percentage elongation of a material from a direct tensile test indicates
explain: Percentage elongation (increase in gauge length at fracture) is the standard measure of a material's ductility.

q: 33. A square column carries a load P at the centroid of one of the quarters of the square, the side of the main square, the combined bending stress will be
explain: Applying combined direct and bending stress formulas for a load placed at the centroid of one quadrant (eccentricity a/4 in both directions) of a square column of side a gives a combined stress of 3P/a².

q: 34. If a shaft subjected to pure torsion cracks, the crack will start
explain: Since shear stress due to torsion is maximum at the outer surface (periphery) and zero at the centre, cracks in a shaft under torsion initiate at the periphery.

q: 35. The bending moment at a section tends to bend or deflect the beam and the internal stresses resist bending. The resistance offered by the internal stresses, to the bending, is called
explain: The internal resisting stress developed within a beam's cross-section to counter the external bending moment is termed bending stress.

q: 36. The neutral axis of a beam is subjected to ............. stress.
explain: Since strain at the neutral axis is zero, and stress is proportional to strain (Hooke's law), the bending stress there is also zero.

q: 37. The ratio of circumferential stress to the longitudinal stress in the walls of a cylindrical shell due to flowing liquid is
explain: For a thin cylindrical shell under internal pressure, circumferential (hoop) stress = pd/2t while longitudinal stress = pd/4t, giving a ratio of 2:1.

q: 38. The tensile test is carried on ............. materials.
explain: Tensile tests (measuring elongation, necking, ductile yielding behavior) are primarily meaningful and carried out on ductile materials.

q: 39. The normal and tangential components of stress on an inclined plane through to the direction of the force will be equal to
explain: For a uniaxial stress acting on an inclined plane, the normal and tangential (shear) stress components become equal when the plane is inclined at 45° to the force direction.

q: 40. Principal planes are subjected to
options: normal stresses as well as tangential stresses
explain: By definition, a principal plane carries only normal stress with zero shear (tangential) stress.

q: 41. If a shaft is subjected to pure twisting moment, an element on the surface is subjected to
explain: Under pure torsion, an element on the surface of a shaft experiences pure shear stress (with associated principal stresses at 45° being tension/compression).

q: 42. When a member is subjected to axial tensile load, the greatest normal stress is equal to
explain: Under uniaxial tension σ, the maximum shear stress is σ/2, so the greatest normal stress (σ) is twice the maximum shear stress.

q: 43. Hooke's law states that stress and strain are
explain: Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 44. For an isotropic, homogenous and elastic material obeying Hooke's law, number of independent elastic constant is
explain: For an isotropic homogeneous elastic material, only 2 independent elastic constants (e.g., E and G, or E and Poisson's ratio) are needed, since all others can be derived from these.

q: 45. Which of the following materials is suitable for transverse test for modulus of rupture?
explain: Timber, being a brittle-ish material in bending with limited ductility, is commonly tested via the transverse (bending) test to determine its modulus of rupture, unlike ductile metals which are usually tested in tension.

q: 46. The lower yield point is more significant than upper yield point because
options: it is less than upper yield point
it is less influenced by shape of the specimen
it occurs before upper yield point
strain is more at this point
explain: The lower yield point is considered more reliable/significant for design purposes because, unlike the upper yield point, it is less sensitive to specimen shape, testing speed, and surface conditions.

q: 47. Struts are load carrying members of a frame structure which are subjected to
explain: A strut is a truss/frame member specifically subjected to axial compressive loads.

q: 48. Which of the following is a proper sequence?
options: Proportional limit, elastic limit, yielding, failure
Elastic limit, proportional limit, elastic limit, failure
Yielding, proportional limit, elastic limit, failure
explain: On a typical stress-strain curve for a ductile material, the sequence of milestones as stress increases is: proportional limit, then elastic limit, then yielding, then eventual failure.

q: 49. The product of the tangential force acting on the shaft and its distance from the axis of the shaft (i.e., radius of shaft) is known as
explain: By definition, the twisting (torsional) moment on a shaft equals the tangential force multiplied by its radial distance from the shaft axis.

q: 50. When a shaft is subjected to a twisting moment, every cross-section of the shaft will be under
explain: Torsion (twisting moment) on a shaft induces shear stress across every cross-section, varying from zero at the centre to maximum at the surface.

q: 51. The shear stress at the centre of a circular shaft under torsion is
explain: Since shear stress under torsion varies linearly with radius (τ = Gθr/L), it is exactly zero at the centre (r=0).

q: 52. When a shaft is subjected to torsion, the shear stress induced in the shaft varies from
options: minimum at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to minimum at the circumference
zero at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to zero at the circumference
explain: Shear stress under torsion in a circular shaft varies linearly from zero at the centre to a maximum value at the outer circumference.

q: 53. A vertical column has two moments of inertia (i.e., Ixx and Iyy). The column will tend to buckle in the direction of the
options: perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: A column buckles about the axis with the minimum moment of inertia (and correspondingly minimum radius of gyration), since that direction offers the least resistance to bending/buckling.

q: 54. The column whose slenderness ratio is less than 80, are known as
explain: Columns with a relatively low slenderness ratio (below about 80) are classified as short columns, where crushing rather than buckling governs failure.
